library.csv lists media items (id, title, duration, type, added). Normalise every row:
- title: remove leading and trailing whitespace and replace every run of internal whitespace with one space; keep the letter case.
- duration: given as H:MM:SS (hours, minutes, seconds), MM:SS (minutes, seconds) or a plain number of seconds. Write it as an ISO 8601 duration PT#H#M#S, leaving out every zero component and using no leading zeros (3725 seconds is "PT1H2M5S", 300 seconds is "PT5M").
- added: given as YYYY-MM-DD, DD.MM.YYYY, YYYY/MM/DD or 'Mon D, YYYY' (English three-letter month). Write it as YYYY-MM-DD.
- type: copy unchanged.
Write catalogue.json as {"items": [{"id": ..., "title": ..., "duration": ..., "type": ..., "added": ...}, ...]}, with items sorted by id ascending and every item value a string.

Your working directory holds library.csv. Commands run there in bash, with python3 and git; there is no network.
evaluate grades catalogue.json with hidden checks; it scores 1 only if every check passes and 0 otherwise.
You have 32 actions in total. Reply with exactly one JSON action object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown.
Run a command: {"action_type": "exec", "command": "sed -n 1,40p library.csv"}
Write a file: {"action_type": "write_file", "file_path": "catalogue.json", "content": "<the whole file>"}
Finish and get graded: {"action_type": "evaluate"}

input.srt is a subtitle file and job.json is the edit sheet for it.
The cues in input.srt are out of order and misnumbered: sort them by start time and number them 1, 2, 3, ...
The cues were timed against source_fps video; the video now runs at target_fps (PAL speed-up), so first rescale every time t to t x source_fps / target_fps, then apply shift_ms.
Then no cue may end later than min_gap_ms before the next cue starts; where one does, move its end time earlier to exactly that point (the gap rule wins over the minimum duration).
Round every time to the nearest millisecond. Keep the text otherwise unchanged.
Write the result to output.srt in standard SRT format (index line, 'HH:MM:SS,mmm --> HH:MM:SS,mmm' line, text lines, blank line between cues).

action_type.description: exec: run a bash command in the working directory and see its output. write_file: write a whole file. evaluate: end the episode; the hidden tests grade your file.
action_type.title: Action Type

content.description: write_file: the complete new file content.
content.title: Content

file_path.description: write_file: the file to write, relative to the working directory.
file_path.title: File Path

reward.description: Reward signal from the last action
reward.title: Reward

state.description:
Base class for environment state.

Represents internal environment state, separate from observations.

episode_id.description: Unique identifier for the current episode
episode_id.title: Episode Id

step_count.description: Number of steps taken in the current episode
step_count.title: Step Count
